🧠 Crypto News Brief: Risk-off mood deepens: Bitcoin clings to $73K as ETF outflows and the sharpest stablecoin contraction since 2022 drain liquidity, and MSCI ejects Strategy. Yet Deutsche Bank and OKXICE keep building institutional rails. 📉 MSCI Confirms Strategy's Removal From Global Indexes MSCI's November review marks Strategy for deletion from its global equity indexes, with Metaplanet and Upexi also cut and Ether treasury firm Sharplink placed on a watchlist. The change takes effect after the Nov. 30 close and could force index-tracking funds to sell; JPMorgan earlier estimated Strategy's exclusion alone could trigger about $2.8 billion in outflows. Read full story 💸 Bitcoin ETF Outflows Hit $1.44B in Five Sessions US spot Bitcoin ETFs shed nearly $300 million on Wednesday, up from $95 million a day earlier, lifting five-day withdrawals to about $1.44 billion. BlackRock's IBIT accounted for $269.7 million of Wednesday's exits and more than $2 billion over nine straight sessions, as Bitcoin hovers near $73,000. More details 🪙 Stablecoin Supply Drops $14.2B in Biggest 30-Day Slide Since 2022 Glassnode data shows stablecoin supply contracted by $14.2 billion over 30 days, the steepest drawdown since June 2022 and larger than the $9.5 billion drop seen in July. Holders are redeeming for dollars and pulling cash from the market, leaving less capital to fuel a rebound, while USDT trades slightly below its peg. Read more 🏦 Deutsche Bank Goes Live With Crypto Custody Germany's largest lender has switched on its Digital Asset Custody service for paying institutional and corporate clients in Europe, covering Bitcoin, Ether, USDC, EURC and EURAU. The bank manages wallets and private keys with hardware-based key protection, multi-person approvals and separate warm and cold storage, with tokenized instruments on the roadmap. See details 🇰🇷 South Korea to Let Exchanges Freeze Withdrawals on Suspected Hacks The Financial Services Commission will issue a no-action letter allowing exchanges to pause deposits and withdrawals when a hack is suspected, not only once it is confirmed. The move follows GOPAX's precautionary suspension and a $70,000 hot-wallet breach at Prabang, and comes with demands for 24/7 monitoring, larger cold-wallet holdings and stronger insurance and reserves.
